title.zh: 卷一百十六 志第六十九 禮十九
title.raw: 卷一百十六 志第六十九 禮十九 Volume 116 Treatises 69: Rites 19

sentences.zh: 禮十九

translations.literal: Rites 19
translations.idiomatic: Rites 19

sentences.zh: （賓禮一）〉

translations.literal: (Guest Rites 1)›
translations.idiomatic: (Guest Rites I)›

sentences.zh: ○大朝會儀常朝儀

translations.literal: ○ Grand Court Assembly Ceremony; Regular Court Ceremony
translations.idiomatic: ○ Ceremonies for Grand Court Assemblies and for Regular Court Audiences

sentences.zh: 《周官》：司儀掌九儀賓客擯相，詔王南鄉以朝諸侯。

translations.literal: The "Offices of Zhou" states: The Director of Ceremonies administers the nine ceremonies for receiving guests and conducting them in and out, and instructs the king to face south to hold court for the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Offices of Zhou, the Director of Ceremonies oversaw the nine ritual forms for receiving guests and guiding them in audience, and directed the king to face south when the feudal lords came to court.

sentences.zh: 「大行人掌大賓之禮、大客之儀，以親諸侯」。

translations.literal: "The Grand Usher administers the rites for great guests and the ceremonies for great visitors, thereby drawing the feudal lords near."
translations.idiomatic: "The Grand Usher was charged with the rites for great guests and the ceremonial forms for great visitors, to keep the feudal lords close to the throne."

sentences.zh: 蓋君臣之際體統雖嚴，然而接以仁義，攝以威儀，實有賓主之道焉。

translations.literal: For although the hierarchical relation between ruler and minister is strict in form, yet they meet with humaneness and righteousness and are governed by dignity and ceremonial decorum—there truly exists the Way of host and guest.
translations.idiomatic: Though the protocol between ruler and minister was strict in outward form, they still met through humaneness and righteousness and were bound by dignity and ritual decorum; in truth there was something of the relationship between host and guest.

sentences.zh: 是以《小雅·鹿鳴》燕其臣下，皆以嘉賓稱之。

translations.literal: Therefore in the "Deer Cry" of the Minor Odes of the Book of Poetry, when feasting his ministers and subordinates, all are styled "honored guests."
translations.idiomatic: Hence in the "Deer Cry" of the Minor Odes, when the lord feasted his ministers below him, he addressed them all as honored guests.

sentences.zh: 宋之朝儀，政和詳定五禮，列為賓禮。

translations.literal: As for the court ceremonies of Song, in the Zhenghe period the Five Rites were determined in detail and were classified as Guest Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song, court ritual was set forth in detail in the Zhenghe reign, when the Five Rites were codified, with these matters placed under Guest Rites.

sentences.zh: 今修《宋史》，存其舊雲。

translations.literal: Now, in compiling the History of Song, we preserve these former provisions thus.
translations.idiomatic: In compiling the present History of Song, we preserve these former provisions as recorded.

sentences.zh: 大朝會。

translations.literal: Grand Court Assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Court Assembly.

sentences.zh: 宋承前代之制，以元日、五月朔、冬至行大朝會之禮。

translations.literal: Song inherited the institutions of previous dynasties and performed the rites of the Grand Court Assembly on New Year's Day, the first day of the fifth month, and the winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: The Song followed earlier dynastic practice and held the Grand Court Assembly rites on New Year's Day, on the first day of the fifth month, and at the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 太祖建隆二年正月朔，始受朝賀於崇元殿，服袞冕，設宮縣、仗衛如儀。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month in the second year of Jianlong under Emperor Taizu, he first received court congratulations at the Chongyuan Hall, wearing the dark ceremonial robe and cap, with palace music and guard of honor arrayed according to the ritual.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the second year of the Jianlong era, Emperor Taizu first received court congratulations in the Chongyuan Hall, wearing imperial full dress, with palace musicians and the guard of honor arrayed as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 仗退，群臣詣皇太后宮門 奉賀。

translations.literal: When the guard withdrew, the assembled ministers went to the gate of the Empress Dowager's palace to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: After the guard of honor withdrew, the ministers went to the Empress Dowager's palace gate to offer their congratulations.

sentences.zh: 帝常服御廣德殿，群臣上壽，用教坊樂。

translations.literal: The emperor, in ordinary dress, took the seat at the Guangde Hall; the assembled ministers offered longevity wishes, and the Music Bureau of the Court Entertainment Office was used.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then appeared in ordinary dress at the Guangde Hall, where the ministers offered longevity toasts, accompanied by music from the Court Entertainment Office.

sentences.zh: 五月朔，受朝賀於崇元殿，帝服通天冠，絳紗袍，宮縣、儀仗如元會儀。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fifth month, he received court congratulations at the Chongyuan Hall; the emperor wore the open-topped cap and crimson gauze robe, with palace music and ceremonial guard as at the New Year assembly.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fifth month he received court congratulations in the Chongyuan Hall, wearing the open-topped cap and crimson gauze robe, with palace musicians and ceremonial guard arrayed as at the New Year assembly.

sentences.zh: 乾德三年冬至，受朝賀於文明殿，四年於朝 元殿，賀畢，常服御大明殿，群臣上壽，始用雅樂登歌、二舞，群臣酒五行罷。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice in the third year of Qiande, he received court congratulations at the Wenhua Hall; in the fourth year at the Chaoyuan Hall. When congratulations were finished, in ordinary dress he took the seat at the Daming Hall; the assembled ministers offered longevity wishes, and for the first time elegant music with elevated song and two dances was used; after five rounds of wine for the ministers, the ceremony ended.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice of the third year of Qiande he received court congratulations in the Wenhua Hall, and in the fourth year in the Chaoyuan Hall. When the congratulations were finished, he appeared in ordinary dress at the Daming Hall, where the ministers offered longevity toasts; for the first time elegant court music with elevated song and two dances was performed, and the ceremony ended after five rounds of wine for the ministers.

sentences.zh: 太宗淳化三年正月朔，命有司約《開元禮》定上壽儀，皆以法服行禮，設宮縣、萬舞，酒三行罷。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month in the third year of Chunhua under Emperor Taizong, he ordered the relevant offices to draw on the Kaiyuan Rites to fix the longevity-wishing ceremony; all performed the rites in formal court dress, with palace music and the myriad dances set out, and the ceremony ended after three rounds of wine.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the third year of the Chunhua era, Emperor Taizong ordered the relevant offices to draw on the Kaiyuan Rites to establish the longevity-wishing ceremony; all participants wore formal court dress, palace musicians and the myriad dances were arrayed, and the ceremony ended after three rounds of wine.

sentences.zh: 真宗咸平三年五月朔，雨，命放仗，百官常服，起居於長春殿，退詣正衙，立班宣製。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fifth month in the third year of Xianping under Emperor Zhenzong, it rained; he ordered the guard dismissed, the hundred officials in ordinary dress performed the audience rite at the Changchun Hall, then withdrew to the main administrative hall, formed ranks, and the edict was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fifth month in the third year of the Xianping era, rain fell; the emperor ordered the guard of honor dismissed, the hundred officials in ordinary dress performed the audience rite at the Changchun Hall, then withdrew to the main administrative hall, formed ranks, and the edict was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 仁宗天聖四年十二月，詔明年正月朔先率百官赴會慶殿，上皇太后壽，酒畢，乃受朝天安殿，仍令太常禮院修定儀製。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Tiansheng under Emperor Renzong, an edict ordered that on the first day of the first month of the following year the emperor should first lead the hundred officials to the Huiqing Hall to offer longevity wishes to the Empress Dowager; when the wine ceremony was finished, he should then receive court at the Tian'an Hall, and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Rites was still ordered to revise and fix the ceremonial regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of the Tiansheng era, Emperor Renzong decreed that on the following New Year's Day he should first lead the hundred officials to the Huiqing Hall to offer longevity wishes to the Empress Dowager; only after the wine ceremony was finished would he receive court at the Tian'an Hall, and he also ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Rites to revise the ceremonial regulations.

sentences.zh: 五年正月朔，曉漏未盡三刻，宰臣、百官與遼使、諸軍將校，並常服班會慶殿。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month in the fifth year, before the third quarter of the dawn watch had passed, the chief ministers, the hundred officials, the Liao envoy, and the military commanders of the various armies, all in ordinary dress, formed ranks at the Huiqing Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the fifth year, before the third quarter of the dawn watch had passed, the chief ministers, the hundred officials, the Liao envoy, and the military commanders of the various armies, all in ordinary dress, formed ranks at the Huiqing Hall.

sentences.zh: 內侍請皇太后出殿後幄，鳴鞭，升坐；

translations.literal: The inner attendants requested the Empress Dowager to come forth from the rear curtain of the hall; the whip was sounded, and she ascended and took her seat;
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants invited the Empress Dowager to emerge from the rear curtain of the hall; the whip was sounded, and she ascended and took her seat;

sentences.zh: 又詣殿後皇帝幄，引皇帝出。

translations.literal: they then went again to the emperor's curtain behind the hall and led the emperor out.
translations.idiomatic: they then went to the emperor's curtain behind the hall and led the emperor out.

sentences.zh: 帝服靴袍，於 簾內北向褥位再拜，跪稱：「臣某言：元正啟祚，萬物惟新。

translations.literal: The emperor, wearing boots and robe, within the curtain bowed twice at the cushion seat facing north and, kneeling, said: "Your subject [name] states: At the New Year the mandate is renewed, and the ten thousand things are all made new.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, wearing boots and robe, within the curtain bowed twice at the cushion seat facing north and, kneeling, said: "Your subject [name] states: At the New Year the mandate is renewed, and the ten thousand things are all made new.

sentences.zh: 伏惟尊號皇太后陛下，膺時納祐，於天同休。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty the Empress Dowager of honored title, having received the age and drawn in blessings, shares felicity with Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty the Empress Dowager of honored title, having received the age and drawn in blessings, shares felicity with Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」內常侍承旨答曰：「履新之祐，與皇帝同之。

translations.literal: " The inner chamberlain, receiving the edict, replied: "The blessings of treading the new year are shared with the emperor."
translations.idiomatic: " The inner chamberlain, receiving the edict, replied: "The blessings of treading the new year are shared with the emperor."

sentences.zh: 」帝再 拜，詣皇太后御坐稍東。

translations.literal: " The emperor bowed again and went to a place slightly east of the Empress Dowager's imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor bowed again and went to a place slightly east of the Empress Dowager's imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 內給事酌酒授內謁者監進，帝跪進訖，以盤興，內謁者監承接之，帝卻就褥位，跪奏曰：「臣某稽首言：元正令節，不勝大慶，謹上千萬歲 壽。

translations.literal: The inner steward poured wine and handed it to the inner usher superintendent to present; the emperor knelt and presented it; when finished, it was raised on a tray; the inner usher superintendent received it; the emperor withdrew to the cushion seat and, kneeling, reported: "Your subject [name], bowing the head, states: On this New Year festival, unable to contain great rejoicing, I respectfully offer ten thousand years of longevity."
translations.idiomatic: The inner steward poured wine and handed it to the inner usher superintendent to present; the emperor knelt and presented it; when finished, it was raised on a tray; the inner usher superintendent received it; the emperor withdrew to the cushion seat and, kneeling, reported: "Your subject [name], bowing the head, states: On this New Year festival, unable to contain great rejoicing, I respectfully offer ten thousand years of longevity."

sentences.zh: 」再拜，內常侍宣答曰：「恭舉皇帝壽酒。

translations.literal: " He bowed again; the inner chamberlain proclaimed the reply: "Respectfully raise the emperor's longevity wine."
translations.idiomatic: " He bowed again; the inner chamberlain proclaimed the reply: "Respectfully raise the emperor's longevity wine."

sentences.zh: 」帝再拜，執盤侍立，教坊樂止，皇帝受虛盞還幄。

translations.literal: " The emperor bowed again, held the tray and stood waiting; the Music Bureau music ceased; the emperor received the empty cup and returned to the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor bowed again, held the tray and stood waiting; the Music Bureau music ceased; the emperor received the empty cup and returned to the curtain.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人引百官橫行，典儀讚再拜、舞蹈、起居。

translations.literal: The communication officer led the hundred officials in lateral procession; the ceremonial director intoned bow twice, dance, and audience.
translations.idiomatic: The communication officer led the hundred officials in lateral procession; the ceremonial director intoned bow twice, dance, and audience.

sentences.zh: 太尉升自西 階，稱賀簾外，降，還位，皆再拜、舞蹈。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant ascended from the western steps, offered congratulations outside the curtain, descended, and returned to his place; all bowed twice and danced.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant ascended from the western steps, offered congratulations outside the curtain, descended, and returned to his place; all bowed twice and danced.

sentences.zh: 侍中承旨曰：「有制。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant, receiving the edict, said: "There is an edict."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant, receiving the edict, said: "There is an edict."

sentences.zh: 」皆再拜，宣曰：「履新之吉，與公等同之。

translations.literal: " All bowed twice; it was proclaimed: "The auspiciousness of treading the new year is shared with you, lords, alike."
translations.idiomatic: " All bowed twice; it was proclaimed: "The auspiciousness of treading the new year is shared with you, lords, alike."

sentences.zh: 」皆再拜、舞蹈。

translations.literal: " All bowed twice and danced.
translations.idiomatic: " All bowed twice and danced.

sentences.zh: 閣門使簾外奏：「宰臣某以下進壽 酒。

translations.literal: The Gate Commissioner reported outside the curtain: "The chief minister [name] and those below present longevity wine."
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Commissioner reported outside the curtain: "The chief minister [name] and those below present longevity wine."

sentences.zh: 」皆再拜。

translations.literal: " All bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " All bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 太尉升自東階，翰林使酌禦酒盞授太尉，執盞盤跪進簾外，內謁者監跪接以進，太尉跪奏曰：「元正令節，臣等不勝慶抃，謹上千萬歲壽。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant ascended from the eastern steps; the Hanlin envoy poured the imperial wine cup and handed it to the Grand Commandant, who held the cup and tray, knelt, and presented it outside the curtain; the inner usher superintendent knelt, received it, and presented it inward; the Grand Commandant knelt and reported: "On this New Year festival, your subjects cannot contain our rejoicing and prostration of joy; we respectfully offer ten thousand years of longevity."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant ascended from the eastern steps; the Hanlin envoy poured the imperial wine cup and handed it to the Grand Commandant, who held the cup and tray, knelt, and presented it outside the curtain; the inner usher superintendent knelt, received it, and presented it inward; the Grand Commandant knelt and reported: "On this New Year festival, your subjects cannot contain our rejoicing and prostration of joy; we respectfully offer ten thousand years of longevity."

sentences.zh: 」降，還 位，皆再拜。

translations.literal: " He descended and returned to his place; all bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " He descended and returned to his place; all bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 宣徽使承旨曰：「舉公等觴。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service, receiving the edict, said: "Raise your cups, lords."
translations.idiomatic: The Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service, receiving the edict, said: "Raise your cups, lords."

sentences.zh: 」皆再拜。

translations.literal: " All bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " All bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 太尉升，立簾外，樂止。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant ascended and stood outside the curtain; the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant ascended and stood outside the curtain; the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 內謁者監出簾授虛盞。

translations.literal: The inner usher superintendent came out from the curtain and handed over the empty cup.
translations.idiomatic: The inner usher superintendent came out from the curtain and handed over the empty cup.

sentences.zh: 太尉降階，橫行，皆再拜、舞蹈。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant descended the steps and moved laterally; all bowed twice and danced.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant descended the steps and moved laterally; all bowed twice and danced.

sentences.zh: 宣徽使承旨宣群臣升殿，再 拜，升，及東西廂坐，酒三行，侍中奏禮畢，退。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service, receiving the edict, proclaimed that the assembled ministers should ascend the hall; all bowed twice, ascended, and took seats in the eastern and western side chambers; after three rounds of wine, the Palace Attendant reported that the rites were finished, and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service, receiving the edict, proclaimed that the assembled ministers should ascend the hall; all bowed twice, ascended, and took seats in the eastern and western side chambers; after three rounds of wine, the Palace Attendant reported that the rites were finished, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 樞密使以下迎乘輿於長春殿，起居稱賀。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and those below met the imperial carriage at the Changchun Hall, performed the audience rite, and offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and those below met the imperial carriage at the Changchun Hall, performed the audience rite, and offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 百官就朝堂易朝服，班天安殿朝賀，帝服袞冕受朝。

translations.literal: The hundred officials went to the court hall to change into court dress, formed ranks at the Tian'an Hall for court congratulations, and the emperor, wearing the dark ceremonial robe and cap, received court.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred officials went to the court hall to change into court dress, formed ranks at the Tian'an Hall for court congratulations, and the emperor, wearing imperial full dress, received court.

sentences.zh: 禮官、通事舍人引中 書令、門下侍郎各於案取所奏文，詣褥位，脫劍舄，以次升，分東西立。

translations.literal: The ritual officers and communication officers led the Director of the Secretariat and the Vice Director of the Chancellery each to take from the table the memorial to be presented, go to the cushion seat, remove sword and shoes, ascend in order, and stand divided east and west.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officers and communication officers led the Director of the Secretariat and the Vice Director of the Chancellery each to take from the table the memorial to be presented, go to the cushion seat, remove sword and shoes, ascend in order, and stand divided east and west.

sentences.zh: 諸方鎮表、祥瑞案先置門外，左右令史絳衣對舉，給事中押祥瑞、中書侍郎押表案入，分詣 東、西階下對立。

translations.literal: The tables of memorials from the various regional commands and of auspicious omens were first placed outside the gate; the left and right clerks in crimson robes raised them facing each other; the Attendant Within the Yellow Gate escorted the auspicious omens and the Vice Director of the Secretariat escorted the memorial table inward, each going to stand facing one another below the eastern and western steps.
translations.idiomatic: The tables of memorials from the various regional commands and of auspicious omens were first placed outside the gate; the left and right clerks in crimson robes raised them facing each other; the Attendant Within the Yellow Gate escorted the auspicious omens and the Vice Director of the Secretariat escorted the memorial table inward, each going to stand facing one another below the eastern and western steps.

sentences.zh: 既賀，更服通天冠、絳紗袍，稱觴上壽，止舉四爵。

translations.literal: When congratulations were finished, he changed into the open-topped cap and crimson gauze robe, raised the cup to offer longevity wishes, and only four rounds of wine were performed.
translations.idiomatic: When congratulations were finished, he changed into the open-topped cap and crimson gauze robe, raised the cup to offer longevity wishes, and only four rounds of wine were performed.

sentences.zh: 乘輿還內，恭謝太后如常禮。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage returned within; he respectfully thanked the Empress Dowager according to the usual rites.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage returned within; he respectfully thanked the Empress Dowager according to the usual rites.

sentences.zh: 元正、冬至大朝會，有司設御坐大慶殿，東西房於御坐之左右少北，東西閣於殿後，百官、宗室、客使次於朝堂之內外。

translations.literal: For the Grand Court Assembly on New Year's Day and the winter solstice, the relevant offices set the imperial seat in the Daqing Hall; the eastern and western chambers slightly north to the left and right of the imperial seat; the eastern and western pavilions behind the hall; the hundred officials, the imperial clan, and guest envoys took their places inside and outside the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: For the Grand Court Assembly on New Year's Day and at the winter solstice, the relevant offices set the imperial seat in the Daqing Hall; the eastern and western chambers slightly north to the left and right of the imperial seat; the eastern and western pavilions behind the hall; the hundred officials, the imperial clan, and guest envoys took their places inside and outside the court hall.

sentences.zh: 五輅先陳於庭，兵部設黃麾仗於殿之內 外。

translations.literal: The five imperial carriages were first displayed in the courtyard; the Ministry of War set the yellow-banner guard inside and outside the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The five imperial carriages were first displayed in the courtyard; the Ministry of War set the yellow-banner guard inside and outside the hall.

sentences.zh: 大樂令展宮架之樂於橫街南。

translations.literal: The Director of Grand Music deployed the palace-frame music south of the cross street.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Grand Music deployed the palace-frame musicians south of the cross street.

sentences.zh: 鼓吹令分置十二案於宮架外。

translations.literal: The Director of Wind and Percussion Music placed the twelve music stands outside the palace frame.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Wind and Percussion Music placed the twelve music stands outside the palace frame.

sentences.zh: 協律郎二人，一位殿上西階之前楹，一位宮架西北，俱東向。

translations.literal: Two pitch-regulating officers: one at the front pillar before the western steps on the hall, one northwest of the palace frame; both faced east.
translations.idiomatic: Two pitch-regulating officers: one at the front pillar before the western steps on the hall, one northwest of the palace frame; both faced east.

sentences.zh: 陳輿輦、御馬於龍墀，傘扇於沙墀，貢 物於宮架南

translations.literal: Imperial carriages and horses were displayed on the dragon terrace, parasols and fans on the sand terrace, and tribute objects south of the palace frame
translations.idiomatic: Imperial carriages and horses were displayed on the dragon terrace, parasols and fans on the sand terrace, and tribute objects south of the palace frame

sentences.zh: （冬至不設貢物）〉

translations.literal: (at the winter solstice tribute objects are not set out)›
translations.idiomatic: (at the winter solstice tribute objects are not set out)›

sentences.zh: ，餘則列大慶門外。

translations.literal: , while the rest were arrayed outside the Daqing Gate.
translations.idiomatic: , while the rest were arrayed outside the Daqing Gate.

sentences.zh: 陳布將士於街。

translations.literal: Soldiers were arrayed along the street.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers were arrayed along the street.

sentences.zh: 左、右金吾六軍諸衛勒所部，列黃麾大仗於門及殿庭。

translations.literal: The left and right Golden Crow guards, the Six Armies, and the various guards mustered their commands and arrayed the great yellow-banner guard at the gate and in the hall courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The left and right Golden Crow guards, the Six Armies, and the various guards mustered their commands and arrayed the great yellow-banner guard at the gate and in the hall courtyard.

sentences.zh: 百僚、客使等俱入朝。

translations.literal: The hundred officials, guest envoys, and the rest all entered court.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred officials, guest envoys, and the rest all entered court.

sentences.zh: 文武常參官朝服，陪 位官公服，近仗就陳於閣外。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials regularly attending court wore court dress; officials in attendance positions wore public dress; the near guard took their stations outside the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials regularly attending court wore court dress; officials in attendance positions wore public dress; the near guard took their stations outside the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 大樂令、樂工、協律郎入就位。

translations.literal: The Director of Grand Music, musicians, and pitch-regulating officers entered and took their places.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Grand Music, musicians, and pitch-regulating officers entered and took their places.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎以諸方鎮表案、給事中以祥瑞俟於大慶門外之左右

sentences.zh: 諸侍衛官 各服其器服。

translations.idiomatic: The inner attendant, receiving the edict, requested the fans; the fans were closed; the emperor wore the open-topped cap and crimson gauze robe.

translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage came forth; the pitch-regulating officer raised the baton and performed the music "Qian'an"; the wind and percussion music sounded vigorously.

translations.idiomatic: The emperor came forth from the western chamber, descended from the carriage and immediately took his seat; the fans were opened; the whip was sounded below the hall.

translations.idiomatic: The pitch-regulating officer lowered the baton and the music ceased; censer smoke rose.

translations.literal: The seal-and-talisman officer bore the seal and placed it before the imperial seat; the Vice Director of the Secretariat and the Attendant Within the Yellow Gate escorted the memorial table and the auspicious-omens table inward and went to stand facing one another below the eastern and western steps; the hundred officials, the imperial clan, and the Liao envoy formed ranks divided east and west, entered in order, the music "Zheng'an" was performed, and they took their places.

sentences.zh: 三師、親王以下及御史臺、外正任、遼使俱就北向位。

translations.idiomatic: The Three Preceptors, imperial princes and those below, the Censorate, regular appointees from outside, and the Liao envoy all took their north-facing positions.

translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant went to below the western steps, removed his sword and shoes, and ascended the hall.

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant went before the imperial seat, knelt facing north, and reported: "The civil and military hundred officials, the Grand Commandant and official [name] and the rest state: At the New Year the mandate is renewed, and the ten thousand things are all made new

translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty the Emperor, having responded to Qian and drawn in blessings, shares felicity with Heaven."

translations.literal: The lateral-procession officials formed ranks and stood.

translations.literal: The Director of the Secretariat and the Vice Director of the Chancellery ascended and went before the imperial seat; each reported the memorials from the various regional commands and the auspicious omens; when finished, the Minister of Revenue went to the position for receiving the edict, bowed prostrate, knelt, and reported the tribute objects from the various prefectures, requesting that they be handed over to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Secretariat and the Vice Director of the Chancellery ascended before the imperial seat and each presented the memorials from the regional commands and the auspicious omens; when they had finished, the Minister of Revenue took the position for receiving the edict, bowed prostrate, knelt, and reported the tribute goods from the prefectures, asking that they be handed over to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書奏諸蕃貢物如之。

translations.literal: The Minister of Rites reported the tribute objects from the various foreign states in the same manner.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Rites reported the tribute goods from the foreign states in the same way.

sentences.zh: 司天監奏雲物祥瑞，請付史館，皆如上儀。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Astronomy reported cloud phenomena and auspicious omens and requested that they be handed over to the Historiography Office; all followed the ritual above.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Astronomy reported cloud signs and auspicious omens and asked that they be sent to the Historiography Office; all followed the procedure described above.

sentences.zh: 侍中進當御坐前奏禮畢，殿上承旨索扇，殿下鳴鞭，官縣撞蕤賓之鍾，左五鍾 皆應，協律郎舉麾，宮縣奏《乾安》樂，鼓吹振作，帝降坐，禦輿入自東房，扇開，偃麾樂止。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant advanced before the imperial seat and reported that the rites were finished; on the hall the edict was received to request the fans; below the hall the whip was sounded; the palace frame struck the bell of the Flaming Guest note, and the five bells to the left all responded; the pitch-regulating officer raised the baton; the palace frame performed the music "Qian'an"; the wind and percussion music sounded vigorously; the emperor descended from his seat; the imperial carriage entered from the eastern chamber; the fans were opened; the baton was lowered and the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant advanced before the imperial seat and announced that the rites were finished; on the hall the edict was received to close the fans; below the hall the whip was sounded; the palace musicians struck the Flaming Guest bell, and the five bells to the left answered; the pitch-regulating officer raised the baton; the palace frame played "Qian'an"; wind and percussion music swelled; the emperor left his seat; the imperial carriage entered from the eastern chamber; the fans were opened; the baton was lowered and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 侍中奏解嚴，百官退還次。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant reported the lifting of strictness; the hundred officials withdrew to their stations.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant announced the lifting of strictness; the hundred officials withdrew to their stations.

sentences.zh: 客使、陪位官並退。

translations.literal: The guest envoys and officials in attendance positions all withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The guest envoys and officials in attendance positions all withdrew.

sentences.zh: 有司設 食案，大樂令設登歌殿上，二舞入，立於架南。

translations.literal: The relevant offices set out food tables; the Director of Grand Music set elevated song on the hall; the two dances entered and stood south of the frame.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices set out the food tables; the Director of Grand Music arranged the elevated song on the hall; the two dance troupes entered and stood south of the music frame.

translations.literal: Those scheduled to take seats who were to ascend the hall took positions before the imperial seat; civil and military officials faced one another in separate ranks with duplicated rows, taking the north as superior; those not ascending the hall took positions below the eastern and western corridors.
translations.idiomatic: Those who were to ascend the hall and take seats stood before the imperial seat; civil and military officials faced one another in staggered ranks, with the north as the place of honor; those not ascending the hall stood below the eastern and western corridors.

sentences.zh: 尚食奉御設壽尊於殿東楹少 南，設坫於尊南，加爵一。

translations.literal: The Imperial Food Service attendant set the longevity wine vessel slightly south of the eastern pillar of the hall, set the altar south of the vessel, and added one cup.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Food Service attendant placed the longevity wine vessel slightly south of the hall's eastern pillar, set the altar south of it, and added a single cup.

sentences.zh: 有司設上下群臣酒尊於殿下東西廂。

translations.literal: The relevant offices set wine vessels for the assembled ministers above and below in the eastern and western side chambers below the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices set out wine vessels for the ministers above and below in the eastern and western side chambers beneath the hall.

sentences.zh: 侍衛官及執事者各立其位，仗衛仍立俟，上壽百官立班如朝賀儀。

translations.literal: Guard officers and those carrying out the rites each stood in their positions; the guard of honor still stood waiting; the hundred officials for the longevity ceremony formed ranks as in the court-congratulation ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Guard officers and ritual attendants each took their stations; the guard of honor remained standing at attention; the hundred officials for the longevity ceremony formed ranks as at the court-congratulation ritual.

sentences.zh: 侍中版奏中嚴、外 辦，聞鳴鞭，索扇，帝服通天冠、絳紗袍，禦輿出東房，樂作。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant reported on the tablet that inner strictness and outer preparations were complete; the whip was heard; the fans were requested; the emperor wore the open-topped cap and crimson gauze robe; the imperial carriage came forth from the eastern chamber; music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant reported on the tablet that inner strictness and outer preparations were complete; the whip sounded; the fans were closed; the emperor wore the open-topped cap and crimson gauze robe; the imperial carriage emerged from the eastern chamber; music began.

sentences.zh: 帝即坐，扇開，樂止。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately took his seat; the fans were opened; the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his seat at once; the fans were opened; the music stopped.

translations.literal: When the intoned bowing was finished, the Director of the Imperial Household went to the south of the cross street, knelt, and reported: "Official [name] states: I request permission for the assembled ministers to offer longevity wishes."
translations.idiomatic: When the intoned bowing was finished, the Director of the Imperial Household went to the south side of the cross street, knelt, and said: "Official [name] requests permission for the assembled ministers to offer longevity wishes."

sentences.zh: 舍人曰「拜」，光祿卿再拜訖，復位。

translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant ascended the hall and went to the longevity vessel, facing north; the Imperial Food Service attendant poured one cup of imperial wine and handed it to him; he inserted his tablet, held the cup, advanced, knelt, and presented it; the emperor took the cup; the Grand Commandant removed his tablet, bowed prostrate, rose, withdrew a step, knelt, and said: "The civil and military hundred officials, the Grand Commandant and official [name] and the rest, bowing the head, state: At the first renewal of the New Year mandate, we cannot contain our great rejoicing and respectfully offer ten thousand years of longevity."

translations.literal: " The intoner said "Bow"; the assembled officials all bowed twice and thrice called "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: " The intoner called "Bow"; the assembled officials all bowed twice and thrice shouted "Ten thousand years."

sentences.zh: 舍人曰：「就坐。

translations.literal: The usher said: "Take your seats."
translations.idiomatic: The usher announced: "Take your seats."

sentences.zh: 」太官令行酒，群官搢笏受酒，宮縣作《正安》之樂，文舞入，立宮架北。

translations.literal: " The Director of the Imperial Kitchen circulated wine; the assembled officials inserted their tablets and received wine; the palace frame performed the music "Zheng'an"; the civil dance entered and stood north of the palace frame.
translations.idiomatic: " The Director of the Imperial Kitchen circulated the wine; the assembled officials inserted their tablets and received it; the palace musicians played "Zheng'an"; the civil dancers entered and stood north of the music frame.

sentences.zh: 觴 行一周。

translations.literal: The cups made one full round.
translations.idiomatic: The cups circulated once around the hall.

sentences.zh: 凡行酒訖，並太官令奏巡周，樂止。

translations.literal: When the wine circulation was finished in all cases, the Director of the Imperial Kitchen together reported that the round was complete, and the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine had circulated in full, the Director of the Imperial Kitchen reported that the round was complete, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 尚食進食升階，以次置御坐前。

translations.literal: The Imperial Food Service presented food, ascended the steps, and placed it in order before the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Food Service brought food up the steps and set it in order before the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 又設群官食，訖，太官令奏食遍。

translations.literal: Food for the assembled officials was also set out; when finished, the Director of the Imperial Kitchen reported that the food had been served throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Food was also set out for the assembled officials; when this was finished, the Director of the Imperial Kitchen reported that everyone had been served.

sentences.zh: 太樂丞引《盛德升聞》之舞入，作三變，止，出。

translations.literal: The Assistant Director of Grand Music led in the dance "Shengde Shengwen," which was performed in three variations, then ceased and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Assistant Director of Grand Music led in the dance "Shengde Shengwen," which was performed in three variations, then stopped and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 殿 中監進第三爵，群官立席後，登歌作《瑞木成文》之曲。

translations.literal: The Palace Domestic Service superintendent presented the third cup; the assembled officials stood behind the mats; elevated song performed the tune "Auspicious Tree Forms Patterns."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Domestic Service superintendent presented the third cup; the assembled officials stood behind the mats; the elevated song performed the tune "Auspicious Tree Forms Patterns."

sentences.zh: 飲訖，樂止。

translations.literal: When he had finished drinking, the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished drinking, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 殿中丞受虛爵，舍人曰：「就坐。

translations.literal: The Palace Domestic Service assistant received the empty cup; the usher said: "Take your seats."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Domestic Service assistant received the empty cup; the usher announced: "Take your seats."

sentences.zh: 」群官皆坐。

translations.literal: " The assembled officials all sat.
translations.idiomatic: " The assembled officials all sat down.

sentences.zh: 又行酒、作樂、進食，如上儀。

translations.literal: Wine was circulated again, music was performed, and food was presented, as in the ritual above.
translations.idiomatic: Wine was circulated again, music was played, and food was served, following the procedure above.

sentences.zh: 太樂丞引《天 下大定之舞》，作三變，止，出。

translations.literal: The Assistant Director of Grand Music led in the dance "Tianxia Dading," which was performed in three variations, then ceased and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Assistant Director of Grand Music led in the dance "All Under Heaven Greatly Settled," performed in three variations, then stopped and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 殿中監進第四爵，登歌奏《嘉禾之曲》，如第三爵。

translations.literal: The Palace Domestic Service superintendent presented the fourth cup; elevated song performed the tune "Fine Grain," as at the third cup.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Domestic Service superintendent presented the fourth cup; the elevated song performed the tune "Fine Grain," as at the third cup.

sentences.zh: 太官令行酒又一周，樂止，舍人曰：「可起。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Kitchen circulated wine for another full round; the music ceased; the usher said: "You may rise."
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Imperial Kitchen circulated the wine for another full round; the music stopped; the usher announced: "You may rise."

sentences.zh: 」百寮皆立席後，侍中進御坐前 跪奏，禮畢，俯伏，興，與群官俱降階復位，讚者曰：「拜。

translations.literal: " The hundred officials all stood behind the mats; the Palace Attendant advanced before the imperial seat, knelt, and reported that the rites were finished; he bowed prostrate, rose, and together with the assembled officials descended the steps and returned to their places; the intoner said: "Bow."
translations.idiomatic: " The hundred officials all stood behind the mats; the Palace Attendant advanced before the imperial seat, knelt, and announced that the rites were finished; he bowed prostrate, rose, and together with the assembled officials descended the steps and returned to their places; the intoner called: "Bow."

sentences.zh: 」皆再拜、舞蹈，三稱萬歲，起，分班立。

translations.literal: " All bowed twice, danced, thrice called "Ten thousand years," rose, and formed ranks standing in divisions.
translations.idiomatic: " All bowed twice, danced, thrice shouted "Ten thousand years," rose, and formed ranks in divisions.

sentences.zh: 殿上索扇，扇合，殿下鳴鞭，太樂令撞蕤賓之鍾，左右鍾皆 應。

translations.literal: On the hall the fans were requested; the fans were closed; below the hall the whip was sounded; the Director of Grand Music struck the bell of the Flaming Guest note, and the bells on both sides all responded.
translations.idiomatic: On the hall the fans were closed; below the hall the whip sounded; the Director of Grand Music struck the Flaming Guest bell, and the bells on both sides answered.

sentences.zh: 協律郎俯伏，舉麾。

translations.literal: The pitch-regulating officer bowed prostrate and raised the baton.
translations.idiomatic: The pitch-regulating officer bowed prostrate and raised the baton.

sentences.zh: 太樂令令奏《乾安之樂》，鼓吹振作。

translations.literal: The Director of Grand Music ordered the performance of the music "Qian'an"; the wind and percussion music sounded vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Grand Music ordered the performance of "Qian'an"; wind and percussion music swelled.

sentences.zh: 帝降坐禦輿入自東房，扇開，樂止。

translations.literal: The emperor descended from his seat; the imperial carriage entered from the eastern chamber; the fans were opened; the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor left his seat; the imperial carriage entered from the eastern chamber; the fans were opened; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 侍中奏解嚴，所司承旨放仗。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant reported the lifting of strictness; the relevant offices, receiving the edict, dismissed the guard of honor.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant announced the lifting of strictness; the relevant offices, receiving the edict, dismissed the guard of honor.

sentences.zh: 百寮再拜，相次退。

translations.literal: The hundred officials bowed twice and withdrew in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred officials bowed twice and withdrew one after another.

sentences.zh: 舊制，朝賀、上壽，帝執鎮圭，至是始罷不用。

translations.literal: Under the old regulations, at court congratulations and longevity offerings the emperor held the stabilizing jade tablet; from this time it was first abolished and no longer used.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old regulations, at court congratulations and longevity offerings the emperor had held the stabilizing jade tablet; from this point it was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 元祐八年，太常博士陳祥道言：「貴人賤馬，古今所同。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanyou, the Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Chen Xiangdao stated: "Honoring men and treating horses as lowly is the same in ancient and modern times."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Yuanyou era, Chen Xiangdao, Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, said: "Honoring men and treating horses as lowly has been the same in every age."

sentences.zh: 故覲禮馬在庭，而侯氏升堂致命。

translations.literal: Therefore in the audience rite the horses were in the courtyard while the marquis ascended the hall to deliver his message.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in the audience rite the horses remained in the courtyard while the marquis ascended the hall to deliver his message.

sentences.zh: 聘禮馬在庭，而賓升堂私覿。

translations.literal: In the mission rite the horses were in the courtyard while the guest ascended the hall for a private audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the mission rite the horses stayed in the courtyard while the guest ascended the hall for a private audience.

sentences.zh: 今元會儀，御馬立於龍墀之上，而特進以下立於庭，是不稱尊賢才、體群臣之意。

translations.literal: Now in the New Year assembly ritual the imperial horses stand upon the dragon terrace while Special Advancement and those below stand in the courtyard—this does not accord with honoring worthy talent or embodying the intent toward the assembled ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the present New Year assembly ritual, however, the imperial horses stand on the dragon terrace while officials of Special Advancement rank and below stand in the courtyard below—this fails to honor worthy talent or embody proper regard for the assembled ministers.

sentences.zh: 請改儀注以御馬在庭，於義為允。」

translations.literal: I request that the ritual regulations be changed so that the imperial horses are in the courtyard; in principle this would be fitting."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the ritual regulations be revised so that the imperial horses stand in the courtyard; that would be proper in principle."

sentences.zh: 舊制，五月朔受朝，熙寧二年詔罷之。

translations.literal: Under the old regulations, court was received on the first day of the fifth month; in the second year of Xining an edict abolished this.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old regulations, court was received on the first day of the fifth month; in the second year of the Xining era an edict abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 元符元年四月，得傳國受命寶，禮官言：「五月朔於故事當大朝會，乞就是日行受寶之禮，依上尊號寶冊儀。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yuanfu, the heirloom seal of receiving the mandate was obtained; the ritual officials stated: "On the first day of the fifth month, according to precedent, there should be a Grand Court Assembly; I request that on that day the ceremony of receiving the treasure be performed, following the ritual for presenting honored-title treasure registers."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of the Yuanfu era, the heirloom seal of receiving the mandate was obtained; the ritual officials said: "On the first day of the fifth month, precedent calls for a Grand Court Assembly; we ask that the ceremony of receiving the treasure be held that day, following the ritual for presenting honored-title treasure registers."

sentences.zh: 」前一日，帝 齋於殿內，翼日，服通天冠、絳紗袍，禦大慶殿，降坐受寶，群臣上壽稱賀。

translations.literal: " On the previous day the emperor fasted within the hall; on the following day he wore the open-topped cap and crimson gauze robe, took the seat at the Daqing Hall, descended from his seat to receive the treasure, and the assembled ministers offered longevity wishes and congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: " On the previous day the emperor fasted within the hall; the next day he wore the open-topped cap and crimson gauze robe, took his seat in the Daqing Hall, descended to receive the treasure, and the assembled ministers offered longevity wishes and congratulations.

sentences.zh: 其後，徽宗以元日受八寶及定命寶、冬至日受元圭，皆於大慶殿行朝賀禮。

translations.literal: Thereafter, Emperor Huizong on New Year's Day received the Eight Treasures and the Mandate-Determining Treasure, and on the winter solstice received the Primordial Gui—all court-congratulation rites were performed at the Daqing Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, on New Year's Day Emperor Huizong received the Eight Treasures and the Mandate-Determining Treasure, and on the winter solstice he received the Primordial Gui—all court-congratulation rites were performed in the Daqing Hall.

sentences.zh: 《新儀》成，改《元豐儀》太尉為上公，侍中為左輔，中書令為右弼，太樂令為大晟府，《盛德升聞》為《天下化成之舞》，《天下大定》為《四夷來王》之舞， 及增刑部尚書奏「天下斷絕，請付史館」，餘並如舊儀。

translations.literal: When the New Ritual was completed, the Yuanfeng Ritual's Grand Commandant was changed to Grand Duke, the Palace Attendant to Left Assistant, the Director of the Secretariat to Right Assistant, the Director of Grand Music to the Dasheng Office; "Shengde Shengwen" was changed to the dance "All Under Heaven Transformed into Patterns," and "Tianxia Dading" to the dance "The Four Barbarians Come as Kings"; and it was added that the Minister of Justice should report "Capital punishment throughout the realm has ceased—please hand this over to the Historiography Office"; the rest all followed the old ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When the New Ritual was completed, the Yuanfeng Ritual's Grand Commandant became Grand Duke, the Palace Attendant Left Assistant, the Director of the Secretariat Right Assistant, and the Director of Grand Music head of the Dasheng Office; "Shengde Shengwen" became the dance "All Under Heaven Transformed into Patterns," and "Tianxia Dading" became "The Four Barbarians Come as Kings"; the Minister of Justice was additionally required to report "Capital punishment throughout the realm has ceased—please record this in the Historiography Office"; everything else followed the old ritual.

sentences.zh: 凡遇國恤則廢，若無事不視朝，則下敕云：「不御殿。

translations.literal: Whenever there was national mourning it was suspended; if there was no pressing business and the emperor did not hold court, an edict was issued saying: "The hall will not be attended."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the state was in mourning the ceremony was suspended; if there was no pressing business and the emperor did not hold court, an edict was issued: "The hall will not be attended."

sentences.zh: 」群臣進表稱賀於閣門。

translations.literal: " The assembled ministers presented memorials offering congratulations at the gate office.
translations.idiomatic: " The assembled ministers instead presented memorials of congratulations at the gate office.

sentences.zh: 紹興十二年十 月，臣僚言：「竊以元正一歲之首，冬至一陽之復，聖人重之，制為朝賀之禮焉。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twelfth year of Shaoxing, a minister stated: "I venture to consider that New Year's Day is the head of the year, and the winter solstice is the return of the single yang; the sages valued these and established them as court-congratulation rites."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the twelfth year of the Shaoxing era, a minister said: "I venture to observe that New Year's Day marks the head of the year and the winter solstice marks the return of the single yang; the sages valued these occasions and established court-congratulation rites for them."

sentences.zh: 自上世以來，未之有改也。

translations.literal: From high antiquity to the present, these have never been changed.
translations.idiomatic: From high antiquity to the present, these have never been changed.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖以五年即位，而七年受朝於長樂宮。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han took the throne in the fifth year and received court at the Changle Palace in the seventh year.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han took the throne in the fifth year and did not receive court at the Changle Palace until the seventh year.

sentences.zh: 我太祖皇帝 以建隆元年即位，受朝於崇元殿。

translations.literal: Our Taizu Emperor took the throne in the first year of Jianlong and received court at the Chongyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Our Taizu Emperor took the throne in the first year of the Jianlong era and received court at the Chongyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 主上臨御十有六年，正、至朝賀，初未嘗講，艱難之際宜不遑暇。

translations.literal: Our sovereign has ruled for sixteen years, yet the New Year and solstice court congratulations have from the first never been performed—in times of hardship it was fitting that there was no leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign has ruled for sixteen years, yet New Year and solstice court congratulations have never once been held—in times of hardship that was only to be expected.

sentences.zh: 茲者太母還宮，國家大慶，四方來賀，亶惟其時。

translations.literal: Now the Grand Empress Dowager has returned to the palace, the state has great celebration, and congratulations come from the four quarters—truly this is the time.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Grand Empress Dowager has returned to the palace, the state celebrates a great occasion, and congratulations arrive from every quarter—surely this is the moment.

sentences.zh: 欲望自今元 正、冬至舉行朝賀之禮，以明天子之尊，庶幾舊典不至廢墜。

translations.literal: I desire that from now on the court-congratulation rites be performed on New Year's Day and the winter solstice, to display the dignity of the Son of Heaven, so that the old regulations may not fall into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that from now on the court-congratulation rites be performed on New Year's Day and at the winter solstice, to display the dignity of the Son of Heaven, so that the old regulations may not fall into disuse.

sentences.zh: 」禮部太常寺考定朝會之禮，依國故事，設黃麾、大仗、車輅、法物、樂舞等，百寮服朝服，再拜上 壽，宣王公升殿，間飲三周。

translations.literal: " The Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices examined and fixed the ritual for court assemblies; according to national precedent they set out the yellow-banner guard, great guard of honor, carriages, ritual objects, music and dances, and the like; the hundred officials wore court dress, bowed twice and offered longevity wishes, proclaimed that the dukes and princes should ascend the hall, and wine was circulated at intervals for three rounds.
translations.idiomatic: " The Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices examined and fixed the ritual for court assemblies; following national precedent they arranged the yellow-banner guard, great guard of honor, carriages, ritual objects, music and dances, and the like; the hundred officials wore court dress, bowed twice and offered longevity wishes, proclaimed that the dukes and princes should ascend the hall, and wine was circulated in three rounds.

sentences.zh: 詔：「自來年舉行。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Perform this beginning next year."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered: "Begin performing this next year."

sentences.zh: 」十一月，權禮部侍郎王賞等言：「朝會之制，正旦、冬至及大慶受朝受賀，係禦大慶殿。

translations.literal: " In the eleventh month, the Acting Vice Minister of Rites Wang Shang and others stated: "In the regulations for court assemblies, the first day of the year, the winter solstice, and great celebrations for receiving court and congratulations all take place at the Daqing Hall."
translations.idiomatic: " In the eleventh month, Wang Shang, Acting Vice Minister of Rites, and others said: "Under the regulations for court assemblies, New Year's Day, the winter solstice, and great celebrations for receiving court and congratulations all take place in the Daqing Hall."

sentences.zh: 其文德、紫宸、垂拱殿 禮制各有不同，月朔視朝則禦文德殿，謂之前殿正衙，仍設黃麾半仗；

translations.literal: The rituals for the Wende, Zichen, and Chuigong halls each differ; for the monthly first-day audience court is held at the Wende Hall, called the front hall and main administrative hall, and a half guard of yellow banners is still set out;
translations.idiomatic: The rituals for the Wende, Zichen, and Chuigong halls each differ; for the monthly first-day audience the emperor holds court at the Wende Hall, called the front hall and main administrative hall, with a half guard of yellow banners;

sentences.zh: 紫宸、垂拱皆係側殿，不設儀仗。

translations.literal: Zichen and Chuigong are both side halls and do not set out ceremonial guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zichen and Chuigong are both side halls and do not set out ceremonial guard.

sentences.zh: 元正在近，大慶殿之禮事務至多，乞候來年冬至別行取旨。

translations.literal: New Year's Day is near, and the ritual affairs of the Daqing Hall are extremely numerous; I request that we wait until the winter solstice of next year to seek separate instructions.
translations.idiomatic: New Year's Day is near, and the ritual affairs of the Daqing Hall are extremely numerous; I ask that we wait until the winter solstice of next year to seek separate instructions.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict approved the request.

sentences.zh: 明年，閣門言：「依汴京故事，遇行大禮，則冬至及次年正旦朝會皆罷。」

translations.literal: The following year the Gate Office stated: "According to the precedent of Bianjing, when a great ritual is performed, the winter solstice and the New Year court assembly of the following year are both suspended."
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Gate Office reported: "According to Bianjing precedent, when a great ritual is performed, the winter solstice and the following New Year court assembly are both suspended."

sentences.zh: 十四年九月，有司言：「明年正旦朝會，請權以文德殿為大慶殿，合設黃麾大仗五千二十七人，欲權減三分之一；

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourteenth year the relevant offices stated: "For the New Year court assembly next year, we request provisionally to use the Wende Hall as the Daqing Hall; the full guard of yellow banners should be 5,027 men, and we wish provisionally to reduce this by one third;"
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourteenth year the relevant offices reported: "For next year's New Year court assembly, we ask provisionally to use the Wende Hall in place of the Daqing Hall; the full yellow-banner guard should number 5,027 men, and we propose provisionally to reduce this by one third;"

sentences.zh: 合設八寶於御坐之東西，及登歌、宮架、樂舞、諸州諸蕃貢物。

translations.literal: the Eight Treasures should be set to the east and west of the imperial seat, along with elevated song, the palace frame, music and dances, and tribute objects from the various prefectures and foreign states.
translations.idiomatic: the Eight Treasures should be set to the east and west of the imperial seat, along with elevated song, the palace frame, music and dances, and tribute goods from the prefectures and foreign states.

sentences.zh: 行在致仕官、諸路貢士舉首，並令立班。

translations.literal: Retired officials at the temporary capital, chief candidates from the various routes in the tribute-student examinations, were all ordered to form ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Retired officials at the temporary capital and chief candidates from the various routes in the tribute-student examinations were all ordered to form ranks.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 十五年正旦，禦大慶殿受朝，文武百官朝賀如儀。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the fifteenth year, he took the seat at the Daqing Hall and received court; civil and military officials offered court congratulations according to the ritual.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the fifteenth year, he took his seat in the Daqing Hall and received court; civil and military officials offered congratulations according to the ritual.

sentences.zh: 常朝之儀。

translations.literal: Regular Court Ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Regular Court Ceremony.

sentences.zh: 唐以宣政為前殿，謂之正衙，即古之內朝也。

translations.literal: Tang took Xuanzheng as the front hall, calling it the main administrative hall—that is, the inner court of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang, Xuanzheng served as the front hall, called the main administrative hall—the inner court of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 以紫宸為便殿，謂之入閣，即古之燕朝也。

translations.literal: Zichen was taken as the convenience hall, called entering the pavilion—that is, the informal court of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Zichen served as the convenience hall, called entering the pavilion—the informal court of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 而外又有含元殿，含元非正、至大朝會不禦。

translations.literal: Outside this there was also the Hanyuan Hall; Hanyuan was not used except for New Year and solstice Grand Court Assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these stood the Hanyuan Hall, used only for New Year and solstice Grand Court Assemblies.

sentences.zh: 正衙則日見，群 臣百官皆在，謂之常參，其後此禮漸廢。

translations.literal: At the main administrative hall one met daily; the assembled ministers and hundred officials were all present—this was called regular attendance; later this rite gradually fell into disuse.
translations.idiomatic: At the main administrative hall the emperor met officials daily; the assembled ministers and hundred officials were all present—this was called regular attendance; later the rite gradually fell into disuse.

sentences.zh: 後唐明宗始詔群臣每五日一隨宰相入見，謂之起居，宋因其制。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong of Later Tang first ordered the assembled ministers to follow the chief minister in audience once every five days—this was called the audience rite—and Song inherited this institution.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong of Later Tang first ordered the assembled ministers to follow the chief minister in audience once every five days—this was called the audience rite—and the Song inherited the practice.

sentences.zh: 皇帝日禦垂拱殿。

translations.literal: The emperor daily took the seat at the Chuigong Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held daily audience at the Chuigong Hall.

sentences.zh: 文武官日赴文德殿正衙曰常參，宰相一人 押班。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials daily went to the main administrative hall at the Wende Hall—this was called regular attendance—with one chief minister supervising the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials went daily to the main administrative hall at the Wende Hall for what was called regular attendance, with one chief minister supervising the ranks.
