translations.literal: If it was announced that the emperor would not take his seat in the front hall, then the chief minister, Commissioner of Military Affairs, Academician of the Hall of Civil Culture, Commissioner of the Three Departments, Hanlin and Military Affairs Direct Academicians, Secretariat Drafter, Vice Commissioner of the Three Departments, Recorder of Imperial Actions, capital officials of the Imperial City Inner Directorate storehouses, various vice commissioners, inner-hall honored guards, inner service officials, attendants-in-waiting, hall attendants, Hanlin medical officials, and awaiting-edict officials entered in the same rank;
translations.idiomatic: If it was announced that the emperor would not take his seat in the front hall, then the chief minister, Commissioner of Military Affairs, Academician of the Hall of Civil Culture, Commissioner of the Three Departments, Hanlin and Military Affairs Direct Academicians, Secretariat Drafter, Vice Commissioner of the Three Departments, Recorder of Imperial Actions, capital officials of the Imperial City Inner Directorate storehouses, various vice commissioners, inner-hall honored guards, inner service officials, attendants-in-waiting, hall attendants, Hanlin medical officials, and awaiting-edict officials entered together;

sentences.zh: 次親王、侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使率軍校至副都指揮使，次使相，次節度使，次統軍， 次兩使留後、觀察使，次團練、防禦使、刺史，次侍衛馬步軍使、都頭，起居畢，見、謝班入。

translations.literal: next imperial princes; the commander of the Palace Guard horse and foot armies leading military officers down to vice commander; next envoy-ministers; next military governors; next army commanders; next two-commissioner acting commissioners and observation commissioners; next training-regiment commissioners, defense commissioners, and prefects; next Palace Guard horse and foot army commissioners and squad leaders; when the audience rite was finished, the audience and thanks ranks entered.
translations.idiomatic: next imperial princes; the Palace Guard horse and foot army commander leading officers down to vice commander; next envoy-ministers; next military governors; next army commanders; next acting commissioners and observation commissioners; next training-regiment commissioners, defense commissioners, and prefects; next Palace Guard army commissioners and squad leaders; when the audience rite was finished, the audience and thanks ranks entered.

sentences.zh: 如禦崇德殿

translations.literal: If holding court at the Chongde Hall
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor held court at the Chongde Hall

sentences.zh: （即紫宸殿也）〉

translations.literal: (that is, the Zichen Hall)›
translations.idiomatic: (that is, the Zichen Hall)›

sentences.zh: 即樞密使以下先就班，候升坐

translations.literal: then those from the Commissioner of Military Affairs down first took their places and waited for the emperor to ascend and be seated.
translations.idiomatic: those from the Commissioner of Military Affairs down first formed ranks and waited for the emperor to take his seat.

sentences.zh: （諸司使 副以下至殿直，分東西對立，餘皆北面。

translations.literal: (Commissioners of the various offices, vice commissioners, and down to hall attendants stood divided east and west facing one another; the rest all faced north.
translations.idiomatic: (Commissioners of the various offices, vice commissioners, and officials down to hall attendants stood east and west facing one another; all others faced north.

sentences.zh: 長春殿皆北面）〉

translations.literal: At the Changchun Hall all faced north)›
translations.idiomatic: At the Changchun Hall everyone faced north)›

sentences.zh: ，宰相、參知政事最後入

translations.literal: , the chief minister and Vice Director of the Chancellery entered last
translations.idiomatic: , the chief minister and Vice Director of the Chancellery entered last

sentences.zh: （以上並閣門讚喝）〉

translations.literal: (all the above were announced by Gate Commissioners)›
translations.idiomatic: (all the above were called out by Gate Commissioners)›

sentences.zh: 日止再拜，朔望及三日假，樞密使以下皆舞蹈。

translations.literal: On ordinary days only double bows were performed; on the first and fifteenth of the month and on the three-day holidays, those from the Commissioner of Military Affairs down all performed the dance bow.
translations.idiomatic: On ordinary days they performed only double bows; on the first and fifteenth of the month and on the three-day holidays, everyone from the Commissioner of Military Affairs down performed the dance bow.

sentences.zh: 早朝，則宰 相、樞密、宣徽使起居畢，升殿問聖體。

translations.literal: At the morning audience, after the chief minister, Commissioner of Military Affairs, and Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service had finished the audience rite, they ascended the hall to inquire after the emperor's health.
translations.idiomatic: At the morning audience, once the chief minister, Commissioner of Military Affairs, and Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service had finished the audience rite, they ascended the hall to inquire after the emperor's health.

sentences.zh: 宰相奏事，樞密、宣徽使退候。

translations.literal: When the chief minister reported on affairs, the Commissioner of Military Affairs and Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service withdrew and waited.
translations.idiomatic: While the chief minister reported on affairs, the Commissioner of Military Affairs and Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service withdrew and waited.

sentences.zh: 宰相對畢，樞密使復入奏事。

translations.literal: When the chief minister had finished responding, the Commissioner of Military Affairs entered again to report on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the chief minister had finished, the Commissioner of Military Affairs entered again to report on affairs.

sentences.zh: 次三司、開封府、審刑院及群臣以次登殿

translations.literal: Next the Three Departments, Kaifeng Prefecture, Court of Judicial Review, and the various ministers in order ascended the hall
translations.idiomatic: Next the Three Departments, Kaifeng Prefecture, Court of Judicial Review, and the other ministers ascended the hall in order

sentences.zh: （大兩省以上領務京 師有公事，許即時請對。

translations.literal: (Officials of the Two Secretariats and above who held duties in the capital and had official business were permitted to request immediate audience.
translations.idiomatic: (Officials of the Two Secretariats and above who held posts in the capital and had official business were allowed to request immediate audience.

sentences.zh: 自餘受使出入要切者，欲回奏事，則聽先進取旨）〉

translations.literal: Others who had been sent out on commission on urgent matters and wished to return and report were allowed to enter first and receive instructions)›
translations.idiomatic: Others sent out on urgent commissions who wished to return and report were permitted to enter first and receive instructions)›

sentences.zh: 其見、謝、辭官，以次入於庭。

translations.literal: Those making audience, offering thanks, or taking leave entered the courtyard in order.
translations.idiomatic: Officials making audience, offering thanks, or taking leave entered the courtyard in order.

sentences.zh: 凡見者先之，謝次之，辭又次之

translations.literal: In general, those making audience went first, those offering thanks next, and those taking leave after that
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, audience came first, thanks next, and leave last

sentences.zh: （出使閑慢或未升朝 官，或止拜於門外，自秘書監、上將軍、觀察使、內客省使以上得拜殿門階上，及升殿止拜御坐前，餘皆庭中班次）〉

translations.literal: (Those on leisurely missions abroad or who had not yet been promoted to court rank sometimes bowed only outside the gate; from the Secretariat Directorate, Senior General, observation commissioner, and Commissioner of the Inner Reception Bureau up, they might bow on the steps before the hall gate, and upon ascending the hall bow only before the imperial seat; the rest took their places in the courtyard)›
translations.idiomatic: (Envoys on leisurely missions or officials not yet promoted to court rank sometimes bowed only outside the gate; from the Secretariat Directorate, Senior General, observation commissioner, and Commissioner of the Inner Reception Bureau upward, they might bow on the hall steps or, upon ascending, bow only before the imperial seat; all others took their places in the courtyard)›

sentences.zh: 惟宰相、親王、使相赴崇德殿，即宣徽使通 喚，餘皆側立候通，再拜舞蹈；

translations.literal: Only the chief minister, imperial princes, and envoy-ministers who went to the Chongde Hall were summoned through by the Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service; the rest all stood to the side waiting to be summoned, then performed double bows and the dance bow;
translations.idiomatic: Only the chief minister, imperial princes, and envoy-ministers proceeding to the Chongde Hall were summoned through by the Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service; all others stood aside waiting to be called, then performed double bows and the dance bow;

sentences.zh: 致辭，即不舞蹈；

translations.literal: when delivering formal addresses, they did not perform the dance bow;
translations.idiomatic: when delivering formal addresses, they did not perform the dance bow;

sentences.zh: 見，即將相升殿問聖體。

translations.literal: When making audience, the chief minister and envoy-ministers ascended the hall to inquire after the emperor's health.
translations.idiomatic: When making audience, the chief minister and envoy-ministers ascended the hall to inquire after the emperor's health.

sentences.zh: 其賜分物酒食及收進奉物，皆舞蹈稱謝

translations.literal: When distributed gifts, wine, and food were granted, and when tribute items were received, all performed the dance bow and expressed thanks
translations.idiomatic: Whenever distributed gifts, wine, and food were granted, or tribute items were received, all performed the dance bow and expressed thanks

sentences.zh: （凡收進奉物皆入謝）〉

translations.literal: (whenever tribute items were received, all entered to offer thanks)›
translations.idiomatic: (whenever tribute items were received, all entered to offer thanks)›

sentences.zh: 幕職、州縣官謝、辭，即 判銓官引對，兼於殿門外宣辭戒勵。

translations.literal: When secretariat staff and prefectural and county officials offered thanks or took leave, the selection-judge official led them in audience, and at the same time outside the hall gate their leave-taking and admonitions were proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: When secretariat staff and prefectural and county officials offered thanks or took leave, the selection-judge official led them in audience, while outside the hall gate their leave-taking and admonitions were proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 凡國有大慶瑞及出師勝捷，樞密使率內職軍校入賀致辭，閣門使宣答；

translations.literal: Whenever the state had great celebrations, auspicious omens, or victorious campaigns, the Commissioner of Military Affairs led inner-service officials and military officers to enter, offer congratulations, and deliver formal addresses; the Gate Commissioner proclaimed the imperial reply;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the state celebrated great felicities, auspicious omens, or victorious campaigns, the Commissioner of Military Affairs led inner-service officials and military officers to enter, offer congratulations, and deliver formal addresses, and the Gate Commissioner proclaimed the imperial reply;

sentences.zh: 宰相致辭，宣徽使宣答。

translations.literal: The chief minister delivered the formal address, and the Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service proclaimed the reply.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister delivered the formal address, and the Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service proclaimed the reply.

sentences.zh: 如賜酒，即預坐官後入，作樂送 酒，如曲宴之儀。

translations.literal: If wine was granted, they entered after the officials already seated, music was performed to accompany the wine, following the ceremony of a private banquet.
translations.idiomatic: If wine was granted, they entered after the seated officials, music was performed as the wine was presented, following the ceremony of a private banquet.

sentences.zh: 晚朝則宰相、樞密、翰林學士當直者，洎近侍執事之臣皆赴。

translations.literal: At the evening audience the chief minister, Commissioner of Military Affairs, Hanlin Academicians on duty, and the close attendants and officials in charge all attended.
translations.idiomatic: At the evening audience the chief minister, Commissioner of Military Affairs, Hanlin Academicians on duty, and the close attendants and executive officials all attended.

sentences.zh: 乾德六年九月，始以旬假日禦講武殿

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the sixth year of Qiande, on the ten-day holidays they first began to hold court at the Jiangwu Hall
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the sixth year of Qiande, the emperor first began to hold court at the Jiangwu Hall on the ten-day holidays

sentences.zh: （又名崇政）〉

translations.literal: (also called Chongzheng)›
translations.idiomatic: (also called Chongzheng)›

sentences.zh: ，近臣但赴早參

translations.literal: , the near ministers attended only the morning audience
translations.idiomatic: , the near ministers attended only the morning audience

sentences.zh: （宰相以下靴笏，諸司使以下係帶）〉

translations.literal: (from the chief minister down, boots and tablet; from commissioners of various offices down, belts worn)›
translations.idiomatic: (from the chief minister down, boots and tablet; from commissioners of various offices down, belts fastened)›

sentences.zh: 其節假及大祀，並令如式。

translations.literal: On festival holidays and at great sacrifices, all were ordered to follow the established form.
translations.idiomatic: On festival holidays and at great sacrifices, all were ordered to follow the established form.

sentences.zh: 開寶九年四月，詔旬休日不視事。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the ninth year of Kaibao, an edict ordered that on the ten-day rest days the emperor would not attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the ninth year of Kaibao, an edict ordered that on the ten-day rest days the emperor would not attend to affairs.

sentences.zh: 及太宗即位，復如舊視朝。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, he restored holding court as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, he restored holding court as before.

sentences.zh: 退進食訖，則易服，禦崇政殿。

translations.literal: After withdrawing and finishing his meal, he changed dress and went to the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: After withdrawing and finishing his meal, he changed dress and went to the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 先群臣告謝，次軍頭引見司奏事於殿下，次三班、審官院、流內銓、刑部及諸司引見官吏。

translations.literal: First the various ministers offered thanks; next the military officers' introduction office reported affairs below the hall; next the Three Ranks, Court of Appointments, Internal Flow Selection Office, Ministry of Justice, and various offices presented officials for audience.
translations.idiomatic: First the ministers offered thanks; next the military officers' introduction office reported affairs below the hall; then the Three Ranks, Court of Appointments, Internal Flow Selection Office, Ministry of Justice, and various offices presented officials for audience.

sentences.zh: 如假日起居辭見畢，即移御坐，臨軒視事。

translations.literal: When holiday audience rites, leave, and audiences were finished, the imperial seat was moved and he held court before the steps.
translations.idiomatic: When holiday audience rites, leave, and audiences were finished, the imperial seat was moved and he held court before the steps.

sentences.zh: 既退，復有奏事，或閱器物之式者，謂之後殿再坐。

translations.literal: After withdrawing, if there were further matters to report, or the forms of utensils to be inspected, this was called a second session in the rear hall.
translations.idiomatic: After withdrawing, if there were further reports or inspection of the forms of utensils, this was called a second session in the rear hall.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，令有司申舉十五條：常參文武官或有朝堂行私禮，跪拜，待漏行立失序，談笑喧嘩，入正衙門執笏不端，行立遲緩，至班列行立不正，趨拜失儀，言語 微喧，穿班仗，出閣門不即就班，無故離位，廊下食、行坐失儀，入朝及退朝不從正衙門出入，非公事入中書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua, the relevant offices were ordered to report fifteen violations: regularly attending civil and military officials who performed private rites in the court hall, knelt and bowed, stood out of order while waiting for the gate to open, talked and laughed noisily, entered the main administrative hall gate holding the tablet improperly, moved and stood slowly, upon reaching their ranks stood improperly, hurried bows were performed incorrectly, speech was slightly noisy, ranks were crossed through the guard formation, upon leaving the gate did not immediately take their places, left their positions without cause, ate or sat improperly in the corridor, upon entering and leaving court did not pass through the main administrative hall gate, or entered the Chancellery without official business.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chunhua, the relevant offices were ordered to report fifteen violations: regularly attending civil and military officials who performed private rites in the court hall, knelt and bowed, stood out of order while waiting for the gate to open, talked and laughed noisily, entered the main administrative hall gate holding the tablet improperly, moved and stood slowly, stood improperly upon reaching their ranks, performed hurried bows incorrectly, spoke too loudly, crossed through the guard formation, failed to take their places immediately upon leaving the gate, left their positions without cause, ate or sat improperly in the corridor, entered and left court without passing through the main administrative hall gate, or entered the Chancellery without official business.

sentences.zh: 犯者奪奉一月；

translations.literal: Offenders had one month's salary withheld;
translations.idiomatic: Offenders had one month's salary withheld;

sentences.zh: 有司振舉，拒不伏者，錄奏貶降。

translations.literal: If the relevant office investigated and reported the violation and the offender refused to accept it, a memorial was recorded and submitted for demotion.
translations.idiomatic: If the relevant office investigated and reported the violation and the offender refused to accept it, a memorial was recorded and submitted for demotion.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，光祿寺丞錢易言：「竊睹文德殿常朝班不及三四十人，蓋以凡掌職務止赴五日起居，頗違舊章。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde, Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Qian Yi said: "I have observed that the regular court ranks at the Wende Hall number fewer than thirty or forty, because in general those holding office attend only the five-day audience rite, which greatly departs from the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingde, Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Qian Yi said: "I have observed that fewer than thirty or forty officials form the regular court ranks at the Wende Hall, because in general those holding office attend only the five-day audience rite, which greatly departs from the old regulations.

sentences.zh: 望令並赴朝參。

translations.literal: I request that all be ordered to attend regular court.
translations.idiomatic: I request that all be ordered to attend regular court.

sentences.zh: 」乃詔應三館、秘書閣、尚書省二十四 司、諸司寺監朝臣內殿起居外，並赴文德殿常參。

translations.literal: " An edict then ordered that apart from the Three Institutes, Secretariat Pavilion, the twenty-four bureaus of the Department of State Affairs, and the various directorates and commissions whose court officials attended inner-hall audience rites, all should attend regular court at the Wende Hall.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict then ordered that apart from the Three Institutes, Secretariat Pavilion, the twenty-four bureaus of the Department of State Affairs, and the various directorates and commissions whose court officials attended inner-hall audience rites, all should attend regular court at the Wende Hall.

sentences.zh: 其審刑院、大理寺、台直官、開封府判官推官司錄兩縣令、司天監、翰林天文、監倉場庫務等仍免。

translations.literal: The Court of Judicial Review, Court of Review, censorial direct appointees, Kaifeng judges, investigators, and recorders, magistrates of the two counties, Directorate of Astronomy, Hanlin astronomical officials, warehouse and depot supervisors, and the like were still exempt.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Judicial Review, Court of Review, censorial direct appointees, Kaifeng judges, investigators, and recorders, magistrates of the two counties, Directorate of Astronomy, Hanlin astronomical officials, warehouse and depot supervisors, and the like remained exempt.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年，御史知雜趙湘言：「伏見常參官每日趨朝，多不整肅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Supervising Censor Zhao Xiang said: "I observe that officials regularly attending court hurry to audience each day, yet many are not properly disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Supervising Censor Zhao Xiang said: "I observe that officials regularly attending court hurry to audience each day, yet many are not properly disciplined.

sentences.zh: 舊制，並早赴待漏院，候開內門齊入。

translations.literal: Under the old system, all arrived early at the waiting-for-the-gate-to-open courtyard and waited for the inner gate to open before entering together.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, all arrived early at the waiting-for-the-gate-to-open courtyard and waited for the inner gate to open before entering together.

sentences.zh: 伏緣每日迨辰以朝，以故後時方入。

translations.literal: Because court is now held close to the chen watch each day, they therefore enter late.
translations.idiomatic: Because court is now held close to the chen watch each day, they therefore enter late.

sentences.zh: 又風雨寒暑，即多稱疾，宜令知班驅使官視其入晚者申奏。

translations.literal: Moreover, in wind, rain, cold, and heat many claim illness; the rank-supervising attendants should be ordered to report those who enter late.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in wind, rain, cold, and heat many claim illness; the rank-supervising attendants should be ordered to report those who enter late.

sentences.zh: 疾者遣醫親視。」

translations.literal: For those claiming illness, send physicians to examine them in person."
translations.idiomatic: For those claiming illness, physicians should be sent to examine them in person."

sentences.zh: 天禧四年十月，中書、門下言：「唐朝故事：五日一開延英，隻日視事，雙日不坐。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Tianxi, the Chancellery and Secretariat said: "Under Tang precedent: Yanying Hall was opened every five days; on odd-numbered days the emperor attended to affairs, on even-numbered days he did not take his seat.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Tianxi, the Chancellery and Secretariat said: "Under Tang precedent, Yanying Hall was opened every five days; on odd-numbered days the emperor attended to affairs, on even-numbered days he did not take his seat.

sentences.zh: 方今中外晏寧，政刑清簡，望準舊事，三日、五日一臨軒聽政，隻日視事，雙 日不坐。

translations.literal: At present within and without the realm all is tranquil, and government and punishments are clear and simple; we request that the old practice be followed, holding court before the steps and hearing government every three or five days, attending to affairs on odd-numbered days and not taking the seat on even-numbered days.
translations.idiomatic: At present the realm is tranquil within and without, and government and punishments are clear and simple; we request that the old practice be followed, holding court before the steps every three or five days, attending to affairs on odd-numbered days and not taking the seat on even-numbered days.

sentences.zh: 至於刑章、錢穀事務，遣差臣僚，除急切大事須麵對外，餘並令中書、樞密院附奏。

translations.literal: As for penal statutes and fiscal affairs, dispatch officials as needed; apart from urgent major matters requiring face-to-face audience, all the rest should be submitted in attached memorials by the Chancellery and Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As for penal statutes and fiscal affairs, officials may be dispatched as needed; apart from urgent major matters requiring face-to-face audience, all the rest should be submitted in attached memorials by the Chancellery and Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 」詔禮儀院詳定，雙日前後殿不坐，隻日視事；

translations.literal: " An edict ordered the Court of Ritual to determine the details: on even-numbered days the front and rear halls would not be occupied, and on odd-numbered days affairs would be attended to;
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered the Court of Ritual to determine the details: on even-numbered days the front and rear halls would not be occupied, and on odd-numbered days affairs would be attended to;

sentences.zh: 或於長春殿，或於承明 殿，應內殿起居群臣並依常日起居；

translations.literal: whether at the Changchun Hall or the Chengming Hall, the various ministers attending inner-hall audience rites should perform audience as on ordinary days;
translations.idiomatic: whether at the Changchun Hall or the Chengming Hall, the various ministers attending inner-hall audience rites should perform audience as on ordinary days;

sentences.zh: 餘如中書、門下之議。

translations.literal: the rest followed the proposal of the Chancellery and Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: the rest followed the proposal of the Chancellery and Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 俄又請隻日承明殿常朝，依假日便服視事，不鳴鞭。

translations.literal: Soon they also requested regular court at the Chengming Hall on odd-numbered days, attending to affairs in ordinary dress as on holidays, without sounding the whip.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they also requested regular court at the Chengming Hall on odd-numbered days, attending to affairs in ordinary dress as on holidays, without sounding the whip.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 康定初，詔中書、樞密、三司，大節、大忌給假一日，小節、旬休並後殿奏事，前後毋得過五班，餘聽後殿對，禦廚給食。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kangding era, an edict ordered that for the Chancellery, Bureau of Military Affairs, and Three Departments, one day's leave be granted on major festivals and major mourning days; on minor festivals and ten-day rest days they should report affairs in the rear hall, with no more than five ranks before and after; the rest might respond in the rear hall, and the imperial kitchen would provide food.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kangding era, an edict ordered that for the Chancellery, Bureau of Military Affairs, and Three Departments, one day's leave be granted on major festivals and major mourning days; on minor festivals and ten-day rest days they should report affairs in the rear hall, with no more than five ranks before and after; the rest might respond in the rear hall, and the imperial kitchen would provide food.

sentences.zh: 假日，崇政殿辰漏，上入內進食，俟再坐復對。

translations.literal: On holidays, at the chen watch at the Chongzheng Hall, the emperor entered to take his meal and waited for the second session before responding again.
translations.idiomatic: On holidays, at the chen watch at the Chongzheng Hall, the emperor entered to take his meal and waited for the second session before responding again.

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong ascended the throne, Censor-in-Chief Wang Tao sent the Huangyou Compiled Statutes' regulations on chief ministers escorting the ranks to the Chancellery, saying that "the Son of Heaven has newly ascended the throne, and the great ministers ought not to abandon court ritual," but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 舊制：祖宗以來，日禦垂拱殿，待制、諸司使以上 俱赴，而百官班文德殿，曰常朝；

translations.literal: Under the old system: from the founding ancestors onward, the emperor held court daily at the Chuigong Hall, and awaiting-edict officials and commissioners of various offices and above all attended, while the hundred officials formed ranks at the Wende Hall, called regular court;
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, from the founding ancestors onward the emperor held court daily at the Chuigong Hall, and awaiting-edict officials and commissioners of various offices and above all attended, while the hundred officials formed ranks at the Wende Hall, called regular court;

translations.idiomatic: every five days all entered, called audience.

translations.literal: On ordinary days, after the chief minister finished reporting affairs at the Chuigong Hall, he went to escort the ranks at the Wende Hall; if the sun had slanted westward and he had not yet withdrawn, the Gate Commissioner would proclaim dismissal of the ranks, and he often did not go again.

sentences.zh: 王陶以韓琦、曾公亮違 故事不押班為不恭，劾之。

translations.idiomatic: Wang Tao impeached Han Qi and Zeng Gongliang for violating precedent by not escorting the ranks, deeming it disrespectful.

translations.idiomatic: On days of audience at Yanying, before the emperor went to the inner hall, dismissal of the ranks was proclaimed, so it is clear that the chief minister did not escort the main administrative hall ranks.

translations.literal: From the founding ancestors onward the emperor held court day after day, and the chief minister reported on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding ancestors onward the emperor held court day after day, and the chief minister reported on affairs.

sentences.zh: 至祥符初，始詔循故事，押文德班。

translations.idiomatic: Only at the beginning of the Xiangfu era was an edict first issued to follow precedent and escort the Wende ranks.

sentences.zh: 以妨職浸廢，乃至今日。

translations.literal: Because it interfered with duties it was gradually abandoned, down to the present day.
translations.idiomatic: Because it interfered with duties it was gradually abandoned, down to the present day.

sentences.zh: 請下太常禮院詳定。

sentences.zh: 」陶坐絀。

sentences.zh: 司馬光代為中丞，請令宰 相遵國朝舊制押班，不須詳定。

translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang replaced him as Censor-in-Chief and requested that the chief ministers follow the dynasty's old system in escorting the ranks, without need for further determination.

sentences.zh: 尋詔：「宰相春分辰初、秋分辰正，垂拱殿未退，聽勿赴文德殿，令御史臺放班。

translations.literal: Soon an edict stated: "At the spring equinox, if before the chen initial watch, and at the autumn equinox, if before the chen proper watch, the chief minister has not yet withdrawn from the Chuigong Hall, he is permitted not to go to the Wende Hall, and the Censorate is ordered to dismiss the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict stated: "At the spring equinox, if before the chen initial watch, and at the autumn equinox, if before the chen proper watch, the chief minister has not yet withdrawn from the Chuigong Hall, he is permitted not to go to the Wende Hall, and the Censorate is ordered to dismiss the ranks.

sentences.zh: 」光又言：「垂拱奏事畢，春分以後鮮有不過辰 初，秋分以後鮮有不過辰正，然則自今宰臣常不至文德殿押班。

translations.literal: " Guang also said: "After affairs are reported at the Chuigong Hall, after the spring equinox it is rare that business is not finished before the chen initial watch, and after the autumn equinox it is rare that it is not finished before the chen proper watch; thus from now on the chief ministers will regularly fail to reach the Wende Hall to escort the ranks.

sentences.zh: 請春分辰正、秋分巳初，奏事未畢，即如今詔，庶幾此禮不至遂廢。

translations.literal: I request that at the spring equinox, if before the chen proper watch, and at the autumn equinox, if before the si initial watch, affairs are not yet finished, then as in the present edict—so that this rite may not be entirely abandoned.

translations.idiomatic: " An edict was then issued that at the spring and autumn equinoxes the standard would be the chen proper watch.

sentences.zh: 熙寧六年正月，西上閣門副使張誠一言：「垂拱殿常朝，先內侍唱內侍都知以下至宿衛行門計一十八班起居，後通事舍人引宰執、樞密使以下大班入，次親王，次 侍衛馬步軍都指揮以下，次皇親使相以下十班入，方引見、謝、辭。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year of Xining, Vice Gate Commissioner of the Western Upper Gate Zhang Chengyi said: "At regular court at the Chuigong Hall, inner attendants first announced eighteen ranks in audience, from the Director of Inner Attendants down to the night-guard procession gate; afterward the communication officer led in the great rank of chief ministers and executive officials, the Commissioner of Military Affairs and below; next imperial princes; next the Palace Guard horse and foot army commander and below; next ten ranks from imperial-clan envoy-ministers down; only then were audience, thanks, and leave ranks led in.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year of Xining, Vice Gate Commissioner of the Western Upper Gate Zhang Chengyi said: "At regular court at the Chuigong Hall, inner attendants first announced eighteen ranks in audience, from the Director of Inner Attendants down to the night-guard procession gate; afterward the communication officer led in the great rank of chief ministers and executive officials, the Commissioner of Military Affairs and below; next imperial princes; next the Palace Guard horse and foot army commander and below; next ten ranks from imperial-clan envoy-ministers down; only then were audience, thanks, and leave ranks led in.

sentences.zh: 或遇百官起居日，自行門後，通事舍人引樞密以下，次親王、使相以下至刺史十班入，方奏兩巡 使起居。

translations.literal: Or on days when the hundred officials performed audience rites, after the procession gate the communication officer led in those from the Commissioner of Military Affairs down, then ten ranks from imperial princes and envoy-ministers down to prefects, and only then were the two circuit commissioners' audience rites reported.
translations.idiomatic: Or on days when the hundred officials performed audience rites, after the procession gate the communication officer led in those from the Commissioner of Military Affairs down, then ten ranks from imperial princes and envoy-ministers down to prefects, and only then were the two circuit commissioners' audience rites reported.

sentences.zh: 立定，方引兩省官入，次閣門引宰臣以下大班入。

translations.literal: When all were standing in place, only then were officials of the Two Secretariats led in; next the Gate Commissioner led in the great rank from the chief minister down.
translations.idiomatic: When all were standing in place, only then were officials of the Two Secretariats led in; next the Gate Commissioner led in the great rank from the chief minister down.

sentences.zh: 起居畢，候百官出絕，兩省班出，次兩巡使出，中書、樞密方奏事，已是日高。

translations.literal: When the audience rite was finished, they waited until the hundred officials had all withdrawn, the Two Secretariats ranks withdrew, then the two circuit commissioners withdrew; only then did the Chancellery and Bureau of Military Affairs report on affairs—by which time the sun was already high.
translations.idiomatic: When the audience rite was finished, they waited until the hundred officials had all withdrawn, the Two Secretariates ranks withdrew, then the two circuit commissioners withdrew; only then did the Chancellery and Bureau of Military Affairs report on affairs—by which time the sun was already high.

sentences.zh: 況大班本不分別丞郎、給 諫、台省及常參官，今獨使相以下曲為分別，虛占時刻。

translations.literal: Moreover, the great rank originally made no distinction among vice directors, drafters, remonstrance officials, censorial and secretariat officials, and regularly attending officials; now envoy-ministers and below alone are artificially distinguished, wasting time.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the great rank originally made no distinction among vice directors, drafters, remonstrance officials, censorial and secretariat officials, and regularly attending officials; now envoy-ministers and below alone are artificially distinguished, wasting time.

sentences.zh: 請遇垂拱殿百官起居日，將親王以下十班合為四班，親王為一班，侍衛馬步軍都指揮使為一班，皇親使相以 下至刺史重行異位為兩班，可減六班，如垂拱殿常朝不係百官起居，或紫宸殿百官起居，其親王、使相以下班，並依舊儀序入起居。

translations.literal: I request that on days when the hundred officials perform audience rites at the Chuigong Hall, the ten ranks from imperial princes down be combined into four ranks: imperial princes as one rank, the Palace Guard horse and foot army commander as one rank, and imperial-clan envoy-ministers down to prefects in double rows with separate positions as two ranks—six ranks may be reduced; if regular court at the Chuigong Hall is not tied to the hundred officials' audience rites, or if the hundred officials perform audience rites at the Zichen Hall, the ranks from imperial princes and envoy-ministers down should all enter for audience according to the old ceremonial order.
translations.idiomatic: I request that on days when the hundred officials perform audience rites at the Chuigong Hall, the ten ranks from imperial princes down be combined into four ranks: imperial princes as one rank, the Palace Guard horse and foot army commander as one rank, and imperial-clan envoy-ministers down to prefects in double rows with separate positions as two ranks—six ranks may be reduced; if regular court at the Chuigong Hall is not tied to the hundred officials' audience rites, or if the hundred officials perform audience rites at the Zichen Hall, the ranks from imperial princes and envoy-ministers down should all enter for audience according to the old ceremonial order.

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Introduction Commissioner Li Duanyin said: "Recently on the first and fifteenth of the month the emperor holds court at the Wende Hall, and in bitter cold and sweltering heat the imperial procession is repeatedly troubled; yet audience at the Zichen Hall is rarely held during the year.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Introduction Commissioner Li Duanyin said: "Recently on the first and fifteenth of the month the emperor holds court at the Wende Hall, and in bitter cold and sweltering heat the imperial procession is repeatedly troubled; yet audience at the Zichen Hall is rarely held during the year.

sentences.zh: 請朔日禦文德，既望坐紫宸，庶幾正衙、內殿朝儀並舉。

translations.literal: I request that on the first of the month he hold court at the Wende Hall, and on the full moon take his seat at the Zichen Hall, so that the ceremonies of the main administrative hall and the inner hall may both be observed.
translations.idiomatic: I request that on the first of the month he hold court at the Wende Hall, and on the full moon take his seat at the Zichen Hall, so that the ceremonies of the main administrative hall and the inner hall may both be observed.

sentences.zh: 元豐八年二月，詔諸三省、御史臺、寺監長貳、開封府推判官六參，職事官、赤縣丞以上、寄祿升朝官在京厘務者望參，不厘務者朔參。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year of Yuanfeng, an edict ordered the vice directors of the Three Secretariats, the Censorate, the directorates and commissions, and the judicial commissioner and administrative assessor of Kaifeng Prefecture to perform six-attendance; duty-holding officials, magistrates of capital prefectures and counties and above, and salary-rank court officials who handled affairs in the capital to perform fifteenth-day-attendance, and those who did not handle affairs to perform first-day-attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year of Yuanfeng, an edict ordered the vice directors of the Three Secretariats, the Censorate, the directorates and commissions, and the judicial commissioner and administrative assessor of Kaifeng Prefecture to attend on six-attendance days; duty-holding officials, magistrates of the capital prefectures and counties and above, and salary-rank court officials handling business in the capital to attend on fifteenth-day-attendance days, and those not handling business to attend on first-day-attendance days.

sentences.zh: 哲宗元祐四年十月，以戶部尚書呂公孺言，詔朔參官兼赴望參，望參官兼赴六參。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Yuanyou under Emperor Zhezong, on a memorial from Minister of Revenue Lü Gongru, an edict ordered first-day-attendance officials also to attend fifteenth-day attendance, and fifteenth-day-attendance officials also to attend six-attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Yuanyou under Emperor Zhezong, on a memorial from Minister of Revenue Lü Gongru, an edict ordered first-day-attendance officials also to attend fifteenth-day sessions, and fifteenth-day-attendance officials also to attend six-attendance sessions.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔權侍郎並日參。

translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, an edict ordered all acting vice ministers to attend daily.

sentences.zh: 紹聖四年十月，御史臺言：「外任官到闕朝見訖，並令赴朔、望參。

translations.idiomatic: Next those below the Bureau of Military Affairs, academicians, drafters in attendance, and chief controllers of the Bureau of Military Affairs; the Director of the Gate together with those below the Attendant Grand Master of Military Merit—the whole rank in unison performs the regular audience rite.

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Henceforth on four-attendance days, when dividing the order of audience ranks, the ranks of palace secretaries and chief ministers and administrators down through the hundred officials may be moved so that they perform the audience rite after the ranks from the Bureau of Military Affairs downward.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "Henceforth on four-attendance days, when dividing the order of audience ranks, the ranks of palace secretaries and chief ministers and administrators down through the hundred officials may be moved so that they perform the audience rite after the ranks from the Bureau of Military Affairs downward.

sentences.zh: 卻令親王並殿前都指揮使以下殿前司員僚，逐班於 宰執以下班後起居，餘並從之。」

translations.literal: Imperial princes and the staff of the Palace Front Service from the Commander of the Palace Front Command downward are instead to perform the audience rite rank by rank after the rank of chief ministers and administrators downward; all the rest follows as before."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes and the staff of the Palace Front Service from the Commander of the Palace Front Command downward are instead to perform the audience rite rank by rank after the rank of chief ministers and administrators downward; all the rest follows as before."

sentences.zh: 淳熙七年九月，詔：「自今垂拱殿日參，宰臣特免宣名。」

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the seventh year of Chunxi, an edict stated: "From now on at daily attendance at the Chuigong Hall, chief ministers are specially exempted from having their names announced."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the seventh year of Chunxi, an edict stated: "From now on at daily attendance at the Chuigong Hall, chief ministers are specially exempted from having their names announced."

sentences.zh: 嘉定十二年正月，臣僚奏：「竊見皇帝御正 殿，或禦後殿，固可間舉，四參官亦有定日。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year of Jiading, ministers memorialized: "We have observed that when the emperor holds court in the main hall or the rear hall, this may appropriately be done at intervals, and four-attendance officials also have fixed days.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year of Jiading, ministers memorialized: "We have observed that when the emperor holds court in the main hall or the rear hall, this may appropriately be done at intervals, and four-attendance officials also have fixed days.

sentences.zh: 近者每日改常朝為後殿，四參之禮亦多不講，正殿、後殿、四參間免。

translations.literal: Recently regular court has daily been changed to the rear hall, the rites of four attendance are largely neglected, and audiences in the main hall, rear hall, and four attendance are frequently skipped.
translations.idiomatic: Recently regular court has daily been shifted to the rear hall, the rites of four attendance are largely neglected, and audiences in the main hall, rear hall, and four attendance are frequently skipped.

sentences.zh: 陛下臨朝之日固未嘗輟，而外廷不知聖意，或謂 姑從簡便，非所以肅百執事也。

translations.literal: The days on which Your Majesty holds court have indeed never ceased, yet the outer court does not know the imperial intent and may suppose this is merely to take the convenient path—this is no way to instill discipline among the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: The days on which Your Majesty holds court have indeed never ceased, yet the outer court does not know the imperial intent and may suppose this is merely to take the convenient path—this is no way to instill discipline among the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 常朝之禮止於從臣，後殿之儀從臣不與，四參止及卿郎，而乃累月僅或一舉。

translations.literal: The rites of regular court reach only attendant officials; attendant officials do not participate in the rear-hall ceremony; four attendance reaches only vice ministers and section officials—yet it is held only once in many months.
translations.idiomatic: The rites of regular court reach only attendant officials; attendant officials do not participate in the rear-hall ceremony; four attendance reaches only vice ministers and section officials—yet it is held only once in many months.

sentences.zh: 咫尺天威，疏簡至此，非所以尊君上而勵百辟也。

translations.literal: The imperial majesty is within arm's reach, yet ritual has been slackened to this degree—this is no way to honor the sovereign and encourage the hundred ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial majesty is within arm's reach, yet ritual has been slackened to this degree—this is no way to honor the sovereign and encourage the hundred ministers.

sentences.zh: 伏願 陛下嚴常朝、後殿、四參之禮，起群下肅謹之心，彰明時厲精之治，豈不偉哉。

translations.literal: We respectfully hope Your Majesty will strictly observe the rites of regular court, the rear hall, and four attendance, rousing reverent diligence among all below and displaying the governance of this bright age forged with vigor—would this not be magnificent?
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully hope Your Majesty will strictly observe the rites of regular court, the rear hall, and four attendance, rousing reverent diligence among all below and displaying the governance of this bright age forged with vigor—would this not be magnificent?

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 初，群臣見、辭、謝皆赴正衙。

translations.literal: At first, when ministers presented themselves, took leave, or offered thanks, all went to the main administrative hall.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when ministers presented themselves, took leave, or offered thanks, all went to the main administrative hall.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，知雜御史張鬱 言：「正衙之設謂之外朝，凡群臣辭、見及謝，先詣正衙，見訖，御史臺具官位姓名以報，閣門方許入對，此國家舊制也。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, Supervising Censor in General Zhang Yu said: "The establishment of the main administrative hall is called the outer court. Whenever ministers take leave, present themselves, or offer thanks, they first go to the main administrative hall; when the audience is finished, the Censorate lists their offices and names and reports them, and only then does the Gate permit them to enter for audience—this is the old regulation of the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua, Supervising Censor in General Zhang Yu said: "The establishment of the main administrative hall is called the outer court. Whenever ministers take leave, present themselves, or offer thanks, they first go to the main administrative hall; when the audience is finished, the Censorate lists their offices and names and reports them, and only then does the Gate permit them to enter for audience—this is the old regulation of the state.

sentences.zh: 自乾德後，始詔先赴中謝，後詣正衙。

translations.literal: From after Qiande, an edict first ordered them to go to the inner thanksgiving audience, then to proceed to the main administrative hall.
translations.idiomatic: From after Qiande, an edict first ordered them to go to the inner thanksgiving audience, then to proceed to the main administrative hall.

sentences.zh: 而 文武官中謝後，次日並赴正衙，內諸司遙領刺史、閣門通事舍人以上新授者亦赴正衙辭謝，出使急速免衙辭者亦具狀報台，違者罰奉一月。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials, after the inner thanksgiving audience, all went to the main administrative hall on the following day. New appointees among honorary prefects of the inner bureaus, communication officers of the Gate and above also went to the main administrative hall for farewell and thanks. Those exempted from hall farewell because of urgent missions also submitted written reports to the censorate; violators had one month's salary forfeited.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials, after the inner thanksgiving audience, all went to the main administrative hall on the following day. New appointees among honorary prefects of the inner bureaus, communication officers of the Gate and above also went to the main administrative hall for farewell and thanks. Those exempted from hall farewell because of urgent missions also submitted written reports to the censorate; violators had one month's salary forfeited.

sentences.zh: 其內諸司職官並將校至刺 史以上新授者，欲望同百官例，赴正衙謝。

translations.literal: For new appointees among inner-bureau duty officials and military officers up to prefect and above, we request that they follow the same practice as the hundred officials and go to the main administrative hall to offer thanks.
translations.idiomatic: For new appointees among inner-bureau duty officials and military officers up to prefect and above, we request that they follow the same practice as the hundred officials and go to the main administrative hall to offer thanks.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 元豐既定朝參之制，侍御史知雜事滿中行上言：「文德正衙之制，尚存常朝之虛名，襲橫行之謬例，有司失於申 請，未能厘正。

translations.literal: After the Yuanfeng court-attendance system was fixed, Supervising Censor in General Man Zhongxing memorialized: "The regulations for the Wende main administrative hall preserve the empty name of regular court and perpetuate the mistaken precedent of lateral procession; the relevant offices failed to petition and could not rectify them.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yuanfeng court-attendance system was fixed, Supervising Censor in General Man Zhongxing memorialized: "The regulations for the Wende main administrative hall preserve the empty name of regular court and perpetuate the mistaken precedent of lateral procession; the relevant offices failed to petition and could not rectify them.

sentences.zh: 兩省、台官、文武百官赴文德殿，東西相向對立，宰臣一員押班，聞傳不坐，則再拜而退，謂之常朝。

translations.literal: Officials of the Two Secretariates, censorial officials, and civil and military officials of the hundred offices go to the Wende Hall, stand facing one another east and west, one chief minister escorts the ranks; when proclamation comes that the emperor will not be seated, they bow twice and withdraw—this is called regular court.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the Two Secretariates, censorial officials, and civil and military officials of the hundred offices go to the Wende Hall, stand facing one another east and west, one chief minister escorts the ranks; when proclamation comes that the emperor will not be seated, they bow twice and withdraw—this is called regular court.

sentences.zh: 遇休假並三日以上，應內殿起居官畢集，謂之 橫行。

translations.literal: When leave totaled three days or more, officials who should attend inner-hall audience all assembled—this was called lateral procession.
translations.idiomatic: When leave totaled three days or more, officials who should attend inner-hall audience all assembled—this was called lateral procession.

sentences.zh: 自宰臣、親王以下應見、謝、辭者，皆先赴文德殿，謂之過正衙。

translations.literal: From chief ministers and imperial princes downward, all who were to be presented, thank, or take leave first went to the Wende Hall—this was called passing through the main administrative hall.
translations.idiomatic: From chief ministers and imperial princes downward, all who were to be presented, thank, or take leave first went to the Wende Hall—this was called passing through the main administrative hall.

sentences.zh: 然在京厘務之官例以別敕免參，宰臣押班近年已罷，而武班諸衙本朝又不常置。

translations.literal: Yet officials handling affairs in the capital were routinely exempted from attendance by separate edict; rank escort by chief ministers was abolished in recent years; and the various military halls of this dynasty were not regularly established.
translations.idiomatic: Yet officials handling affairs in the capital were routinely exempted from attendance by separate edict; rank escort by chief ministers was abolished in recent years; and the various military halls of this dynasty were not regularly established.

sentences.zh: 故今之赴常 朝者，獨御史臺官與審官、待次階官而已。

translations.literal: Thus those who now attend regular court are only censorate officials and officials of the Court for Reviewing Offices and officials awaiting assignment by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Thus those who now attend regular court are only censorate officials and officials of the Court for Reviewing Offices and officials awaiting assignment by rank.

sentences.zh: 今垂拱內殿宰臣以下既已日參，而文德常朝仍復不廢，舛謬倒置，莫此為甚。

translations.literal: Now chief ministers and those below already perform daily attendance in the inner hall at Chuigong, yet regular court at Wende has still not been abolished—nothing is more confused and inverted than this.
translations.idiomatic: Now chief ministers and those below already perform daily attendance in the inner hall at Chuigong, yet regular court at Wende has still not been abolished—nothing is more confused and inverted than this.

sentences.zh: 至於橫行參假，與夫見、謝、辭官先過正 衙，雖沿唐之故事，然必俟天子御殿之日行之可也。

translations.literal: As for lateral-procession leave reporting, and officials for presentation, thanks, and farewell first passing through the main administrative hall—although these follow Tang precedent, they should be carried out only on days when the Son of Heaven holds court.
translations.idiomatic: As for lateral-procession leave reporting, and officials for presentation, thanks, and farewell first passing through the main administrative hall—although these follow Tang precedent, they should be carried out only on days when the Son of Heaven holds court.

sentences.zh: 」詔下詳定官制所。

translations.literal: " The edict was sent down to the Office for Determining the Official System in Detail.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict was sent down to the Office for Determining the Official System in Detail.

sentences.zh: 言：「今天子日聽政於垂拱，以接執政官及內朝之臣，而更於別殿宣敕不坐，實為因習之 誤。

translations.literal: It reported: "Today the Son of Heaven daily hears governance at Chuigong to receive the chief administering officials and inner-court ministers, yet proclamation is still made in a separate hall that he will not be seated—this is truly a lingering mistake of custom.
translations.idiomatic: It reported: "Today the Son of Heaven daily hears governance at Chuigong to receive the chief administering officials and inner-court ministers, yet proclamation is still made in a separate hall that he will not be seated—this is truly a lingering mistake of custom.

sentences.zh: 兼有執事升朝官五日一赴起居，而未有執事者反謂之參，疏數之節尤為未當。

translations.literal: Moreover, duty-holding court officials attend audience every five days, while those without duties are instead called attendants—the rhythm of frequency and spacing is especially inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, duty-holding court officials attend audience every five days, while those without duties are instead called attendants—the rhythm of frequency and spacing is especially inappropriate.

sentences.zh: 又辭、見、謝，自已入見天子，則前殿正衙對拜為虛文。

translations.literal: Further, for farewell, presentation, and thanks, since one has already entered to see the Son of Heaven, the reciprocal bows at the front-hall main administrative hall become empty form.
translations.idiomatic: Further, for farewell, presentation, and thanks, since one has already entered to see the Son of Heaven, the reciprocal bows at the front-hall main administrative hall become empty form.

sentences.zh: 其連遇朝假，則百官司赴 大起居，不當復有橫行參假。

translations.literal: When court holidays follow in succession, the hundred offices attend the great audience rite; there should be no further lateral-procession leave reporting.
translations.idiomatic: When court holidays follow in succession, the hundred offices attend the great audience rite; there should be no further lateral-procession leave reporting.

sentences.zh: 宜如中行言。

translations.literal: The recommendation of Zhongxing should be followed.
translations.idiomatic: The recommendation of Zhongxing should be followed.

sentences.zh: 」於是常朝、正衙、橫行之儀俱罷。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the ceremonies of regular court, the main administrative hall, and lateral procession were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the ceremonies of regular court, the main administrative hall, and lateral procession were all abolished.
